result:
I shipped both of my sub-tasks, PLAT-104-3 (core shell) and PLAT-104-4 (reports), in one PR. PR #3 is merged, and CI and CD both passed on main. I haven't checked the deployed pages themselves.

- **What changed:** `shared-contracts` lives in `libs/` and is inlined at build time, so there was no registry version to bump. CD only rebuilds an app when files under its own `apps/` directory change. I bumped `core-shell` and `sub-route-reports` from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 so CD rebuilt both with dev-a's `billingUrl` of `https://homelab.local/billing/v2`.
- **Coordination:** I waited for dev-a's handoff note, which said the lib change was merged to main and that my apps needed a change under their own directories. I didn't need to post a note myself, since nothing depends on my work. I checked that the lib on main has the new URL before opening the PR.
- **Surprises:**
  - The ticket's wording ("adopt the new release") suggests a dependency update, which doesn't apply here. The handoff note and `docs/ci-cd.md` are what clarified it.
  - `docs/ci-cd.md` says CD deploys are switched off, but the baseline commit has them on.
  - `docs/releasing.md` lists only the shell and billing as deployed components, yet `Jenkinsfile.cd` also handles reports.

I ran `done` with my assumptions. The main one is that one combined PR was acceptable, because the two apps don't need to land in a particular order.
